newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan says coalition seeks early polls.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan says coalition seeks early polls.

text.p: Turkey' Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Sunday that his crumbling 11-month-old coalition with conservatives had decided to seek early elections to solve a government crisis.
"We decided that for Turkey to continue its economic success, an early election would be necessary," Erbakan told a news conference.

Erbakan's party has has been locked in bargaining with Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's True Path Party (DYP) over a possible date for early elections, which must be approved by parliament. A DYP minister has said elections could be held as early as October.
Erbakan said the coalition protocol signed with the conservative DYP last June envisaged handing over the premiership to the DYP in the case of snap elections.
"Our protocol proposes that the premiership be handed over to the other partner if Turkey needs to go for an early election after one year (from June 1996)," Erbakan said.
Ciller has promised her party she would press Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, to let her lead the country to polls as caretaker head of government.
